cut_items.item: localStorage is acceptable for low-risk apps (internal tool, prototype); use cookies for sensitive data, payments, admin roles
Cross-domain API with cookies requires CORS with credentials; BFF avoids this
Recommends SameSite=Lax cookie for server-set session/JWT as concrete setup
localStorage is acceptable for low-risk apps such as internal tools or prototypes, while sensitive data, payments or admin roles warrant cookies
Cookie-based setup with a separate API domain needs CORS with credentials; BFF avoids this
Server can set the JWT itself as an HttpOnly cookie as a simple alternative

added_items.item: Concrete SPA pattern: access token in JS memory only, refresh token in HttpOnly cookie scoped to the refresh endpoint, call refresh on page load to get new access token
Rotate refresh tokens on each use and revoke the token family on reuse
Check Origin header as a CSRF defence alternative to CSRF token
Explains that localStorage is readable by all scripts including npm dependencies and analytics, and that the victim need not be online for the stolen token to work
Refresh token rotation with revocation of the whole token family on reuse detection
Concrete SPA pattern: access token in JS memory only, refresh token in HttpOnly cookie scoped to refresh endpoint, call refresh on page load
Explains cookie flag meanings (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite Lax/Strict) and checking Origin header as CSRF defense

Explains why localStorage is risky: readable by npm deps and analytics, no expiry, no HttpOnly
